items.note: Groups ran brainwriting ideation with an LLM added and the authors evaluated the resulting solution space (expert and novice ratings, plus an LLM evaluation engine); the abstract does not state a no-AI comparison condition or sample size, so the full text must confirm whether a human-only round or group exists (else system_paper_no_comparison); arXiv 2402.14978 is the same paper.

Title suggests a study varying the mediation mode of group collaboration with an AI co-ideation peer; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex and Crossref have none, Semantic Scholar 404, SSRN 403, web search found nothing), so design, sample, and outcomes are unverified; same author team as c904.

Controlled experiments in India and the US where people wrote constructive comments on divisive threads alone or with an LLM, with comments rated for constructiveness; the 600 is the total across experiments (search notes say the writing experiment randomized 104 people and measured cross-writer similarity and lexical diversity, which the full text must confirm); constructiveness is not creativity, so eligibility rests on the across_people diversity outcome.

Between-subjects study (N=24) comparing an AI design-ideation interface that reads sketches plus concurrent speech with sketch-only input; the abstract reports perceived alignment and creativity support, not scored design outputs, and the sample is below 50.

Research-in-progress pilot comparing voice with text interaction with generative AI in rule-bound co-creation tasks, finding lower output quality with voice; the task is described as rule-bound, so whether it is a creative or ideation task, and the pilot's sample size, need checking in the full text (abstract from the AIS eLibrary page).

Forty-eight participants generated and selected ideas with one of two facilitator chatbots (structured versus adaptive process), an AI-configuration comparison with no no-AI arm; the abstract does not say idea quality was scored, and the sample is below 50; arXiv 2503.03617 is the same paper.
Thirty designers worked on bio-inspired design tasks in three modes (BID stimuli only, ChatGPT only, both) and creativity was measured only through EEG task-related power, not by scoring the designs.

CHI extended abstract manipulating interaction depth and suggestion phrasing in AI-assisted narrative planning against a human-only baseline, with preliminary results showing more original story ideas with AI; sample size and assignment not stated.

Small-scale user study comparing a node-based visual graph system for chaining generative models with a conversational interface on creative writing; outcomes appear qualitative or self-reported and the sample is small, so it will likely fail at full text.

Experiment with 90 participants generating new venture ideas with or without an AI system, finding more creative, novel, and useful ideas but lower average novelty with AI; the abstract does not name the AI system, and a 2022 study may predate generative AI, so the full text must confirm the tool is generative (else not_generative_ai).
